summary.oneLiner: Cupid Limited is transitioning from a low-margin latex condom exporter to a diversified reproductive health player through strategic overseas acquisitions of non-latex condom manufacturing capabilities and IVD product approvals, with near-term revenue upside from backlog execution and FY25 capacity expansion. The company's path to profitability hinges on resolving South African logistics, securing USFDA approval, and converting order book into revenue.
summary.business: Incorporated in 1993 and manufacturing from Sinnar near Nashik in Maharashtra, Cupid makes latex male condoms, natural-rubber-latex female condoms, rapid in-vitro diagnostic test kits and water-based lubricants, with every condom electronically tested before dispatch. The company describes itself as running on two engines powered by one manufacturing, research and quality platform: a global institutional B2B franchise selling into international tenders, public-health programmes and OEM/private-label relationships, and a consumer B2C business launched in FY2024 spanning condoms, lubricants, diagnostics and a widening FMCG personal-care, beauty and hygiene range sold through distributors, modern trade, organised retail and e-commerce in India. Customers include ministries of health, multilateral agencies and institutions such as WHO/UNFPA, PFSCM, the Global Fund, MSI, PSI and the IDA Foundation, alongside Indian wholesalers and retailers.

Male condoms: Latex male condoms varied in texture, flavour, shape and size
Flavoured and dotted condoms (launched during FY2026)
Female condoms: Nitrile (NBR) latex-free female condom (development commenced in FY2026)
FMCG, personal care and wellness: Cupid (premium sexual wellness, fragrances, lubricants, personal care and hygiene)
Angel / Cupid Angel (women's sexual wellness, fragrances, body care and beauty)
Eau de parfums, deodorants and pocket perfumes
Face wash, hair-removal sprays, hair and body oils, almond hair oil, petroleum jelly
Talcum powder, sunscreen, shower gels, body mists, hand washes and colour cosmetics (launched during FY2026)

currentContext.strengths: Regulatory pre-qualification as an entry barrier: first company in the world to earn WHO/UNFPA pre-qualification for both male and female condoms, a credential described as central to the institutional business|Rare global position in female condoms - one of only a handful of manufacturers worldwide, supplying more than 50 countries|Three decades of institutional relationships with governments, ministries of health, UN agencies and procurement bodies, supporting repeat tender participation across 125+ countries|Fully integrated manufacturing with electronic testing of every condom and GMP-compliant systems accepted by drug regulators worldwide|OEM capability positioned under the 'Made in India with Japanese Quality' initiative|One manufacturing, research and quality platform serving two engines - the same certifications that win institutional tenders underwrite the consumer brands|Deep and widening FMCG distribution: more than 1.5 lakh retail outlets nationwide including over 75,000 chemists and over 47,000 cosmetics outlets, plus over 2,900 modern-trade stores listed and an e-commerce channel that serviced over 52,000 orders|Balance-sheet strength and supply security - modest borrowings, a net-cash position, and raw-material inventory including crude-linked inputs held for well over six months to protect execution and margins|CE (EU IVDR) certification broadening eligibility for regulated markets and multilateral health tenders
currentContext.strategies: Run the business as two engines on one platform of manufacturing, research and quality - a global institutional B2B franchise as the anchor of credibility, regulatory approvals and stability, and a fast-scaling B2C consumer business built directly on that foundation.|Grow the consumer business into the scale engine that management expects, over time, to grow beyond the core export business in size, while exports continue to provide resilience.|Enter the premium end of the female-condom market by developing a latex-free nitrile (NBR) female condom for a global market historically served by a single supplier, a segment with high technical and regulatory barriers to entry.|Build the new Palava plant with integrated dual-polymer lines as the principal growth investment, to become the only Indian manufacturer across male, female and nitrile female condoms.|Use CE (EU IVDR) certification of the diagnostic kits to open regulated markets such as the European Economic Area and strengthen eligibility for multilateral health tenders.|Scale the FMCG portfolio through multi-brand launches and deeper omnichannel distribution - chemists, cosmetics, groceries, pan-plus and open-format stores, modern trade and e-commerce - accelerated by the strategic investment in Baazar Style Retail.|Maintain a geographically diversified customer base and long-standing institutional relationships that are less sensitive to short-term cycles, as protection against tariff and trade uncertainty.|Manage input costs deliberately by holding raw-material inventory, including crude-linked inputs, comfortably for well over six months to support uninterrupted execution and margin resilience.|Manage currency as a two-way risk through natural hedging and pricing discipline.|Continue R&D and technology upgradation focused on product and process improvement, regulatory compliance and cost competitiveness across domestic and international markets.
currentContext.expansion: Cupid's principal growth investment is a new plant at Palava, purpose-built with integrated dual-polymer dipping lines for both natural-rubber-latex and nitrile products. The Executive Director describes Palava as India's first facility capable of manufacturing both natural rubber latex and nitrile condoms on dedicated production lines, while natural rubber latex continues to account for the overwhelming majority of production; the nitrile capability is intended to open a long-term opportunity in the global female-condom market. On full commissioning, total capacity is expected to rise towards approximately 1.25 billion male and 125 million female condoms a year, which management says would make Cupid the only Indian manufacturer across male, female and nitrile female condoms. The stated FY2027 operational priority is to commission the Palava facility on schedule during FY27, alongside establishing the nitrile female condom platform and preparing it for regulated global markets; execution risk on capacity expansion is mitigated by phased commissioning supported by established manufacturing expertise. The established facility at Sinnar, near Nashik, remains the operating base, running GMP-compliant quality-management systems with every condom electronically tested before dispatch. Expansion of market access is being pursued through strategic investments rather than plant alone - the Baazar Style Retail partnership and the GII Healthcare Fund are described as disciplined investments to strengthen market access and expand distribution. Supply security is managed by holding raw-material inventory, including crude-linked inputs, comfortably for well over six months. The annual report gives no rupee capex quantum for Palava in the narrative, and the capital-commitments named disclosure supplied carries no attributable figure.
currentContext.mdna: The global condom market is expected to grow at a CAGR of about 8.7% between FY23-30, driven by rising awareness of HIV and other sexually transmitted infections, family-planning programmes and expanding retail and e-commerce access; Asia-Pacific is the largest market at roughly half of global revenue and latex remains the dominant material.|The female condom market is estimated at approximately 770 million in 2026, growing to around 1.2 billion by 2030, and is increasingly segmenting by material - latex, polyurethane and, at the premium end, nitrile.|Nitrile products typically command 25-35% higher pricing than latex, the direction in which the company is investing.|India's IVD market was estimated by IMARC at approximately US$5.3 billion in 2024, growing to around US$10.0 billion by 2033, driven by rising chronic and infectious disease, health awareness, diagnostic access in smaller towns and rural areas, and government focus on public health.|India's FMCG market was estimated at approximately US$289 billion in 2025 and is expected to reach around US$643 billion by 2030, a CAGR of roughly 17%, with personal care and health-and-wellness among the fastest-growing categories.|GST rationalisation and simplification together with personal income-tax relief are expected to put more money in the hands of consumers and support demand for everyday products of the kind being built in the consumer business; rural demand showed signs of a durable recovery and inflation remained benign.|A generally firmer US Dollar against the Indian Rupee supported the reported realisations of exporters, although currency is acknowledged as a two-way risk.|Operating leverage is the stated margin lever: as volumes scaled, the cost base grew far more slowly, and a favourable export-realisation environment supported margins; management expects margins to remain healthy as scale builds, while noting that quarter-to-quarter mix and the timing of large institutional orders can cause variability.|Richer product mix and broad-based volume growth across both export and domestic businesses were cited as the drivers of the year's growth.|A marked increase in tariffs and protectionist measures, and the uncertainty they created, weighed on investment and external demand in several regions - reinforcing the value of a geographically diversified customer base for an export-oriented business.|Holding raw-material inventory, including crude-linked inputs, for well over six months supports uninterrupted execution and margin resilience.|CE (EU IVDR) certifications obtained during the year strengthen eligibility for regulated markets and institutional programmes.|Our institutional order pipeline across government and UN-agency programmes is the strongest it has been.|Global tenders and institutional demand is listed as an opportunity: a strong and growing order pipeline across governments and UN agencies, supported by pre-qualification status and track record.|The timing of large institutional orders is flagged as a source of quarter-to-quarter variability, alongside customer and tender concentration in the institutional business.

risks.note: Listed as a principal risk in the MD&A: movements in crude-linked and other key raw-material costs feed directly into the cost base of a latex and polymer manufacturer. Management mitigates it by holding more than six months of raw-material cover and through inflation-linked price revisions, which itself ties up working capital - inventory carried was higher at the year-end for exactly this reason.

risks.risk: Currency movement on a heavily export-weighted revenue base
risks.note: Exports were approximately 59.3% of revenue from operations in FY2026, so realisations swing with the rupee. Management calls currency a tailwind in the current period but a genuine two-way risk, managed through natural hedging and pricing discipline; a favourable currency environment was explicitly named as one of the drivers of the FY2026 margin expansion, meaning a reversal would work the other way.

risks.risk: Customer and tender concentration in the institutional business
risks.note: The B2B franchise sells into a small number of governments, UN agencies and procurement bodies through large tenders, so both the winning of individual tenders and the timing of large orders matter. Management notes that quarter-to-quarter mix and the timing of large institutional orders can cause variability, and addresses the risk through diversification across geographies and channels and the growth of the domestic business.

risks.risk: Execution of the Palava ramp-up and the nitrile programme
risks.note: The principal growth investment is a new plant whose capacity is expected to rise towards approximately 1.25 billion male and 125 million female condoms a year, alongside an entirely new nitrile (NBR) product platform. Slippage in commissioning or in the nitrile ramp would defer the capacity and mix benefits on which the growth plan rests; management says it is managed through phased commissioning and established manufacturing discipline.

risks.risk: Regulatory change and evolving quality/certification requirements across many markets
risks.note: The institutional business depends on WHO/UNFPA pre-qualification and CE (EU IVDR) certification - credentials that are the licence to bid rather than a marketing claim. Regulatory change across the many markets served, and evolving quality and certification requirements, is flagged in the MD&A threat list; BRSR separately identifies environmental compliance as a risk where non-compliance could expose the Company to legal action, operational disruption and reputational damage.

risks.risk: Consumer/FMCG scale-up requires investment ahead of returns
risks.note: The second engine, launched only in FY2024, is being scaled through brand building, new product launches and distribution across more than 1.5 lakh outlets plus an investment in Baazar Style Retail. The MD&A explicitly flags scaling a consumer business that requires investment ahead of returns as part of its execution risk, and the current ratio fell sharply during the year owing to long-term strategic investment and capex.

The MD&A discloses that the promoter share-pledge was reduced to 34.26% during the year - a reduction, but a still-material portion of promoter holding (promoter and promoter group held approximately 46.03% of equity as on 31 March 2026) remains pledged, which is a structural overhang tied to promoter-level financing rather than to operations.

risks.risk: Occupational health, safety and hazardous-waste/fire exposure at manufacturing sites
risks.note: BRSR identifies occupational health and safety, hazardous waste management and fire and emergency preparedness as material risks, each with a negative financial implication if unmanaged - workplace injuries, regulatory penalties, environmental contamination, asset damage and business disruption. Mitigations cited are HIRA, permit-to-work systems, PPE, periodic safety audits, disposal only through authorised recyclers with Form-3/manifest documentation, and regular mock drills and fire-safety inspections.

one-line thesis: Cupid Limited is transitioning from a low-margin latex condom exporter to a diversified reproductive health player through strategic overseas acquisitions of non-latex condom manufacturing capabilities and IVD product approvals, with near-term revenue upside from backlog execution and FY25 capacity expansion. The company's path to profitability hinges on resolving South African logistics, securing USFDA approval, and converting order book into revenue.
financial scorecard: rev: +16% QoQ; EBITDA: 30.33%; PAT: +73% QoQ; orderbook: Rs.80Cr; netdebt: net cash position (no debt mentioned)
guidance: Q4FY24 topline: Rs.50-55Cr; female condom sales: Rs.21Cr; FY24 total revenue: ~Rs.160Cr; FY25 topline target: Rs.400Cr; EBITDA: >Rs.100Cr post-capacity expansion
order book & pipeline: Rs.80Cr total (Rs.50Cr male condoms; Rs.30Cr female condoms); 85-90% international, 10-15% domestic; key buyers: UNFPA, Brazilian government (Rs.23Cr tender expected), Government of India (Rs.15Cr awarded + Rs.10Cr expected), South Africa (Rs.50Cr 3-year contract)
segment / subsidiary detail: Male condoms: 89% of Q3 sales, 480M unit capacity, expanding to 780M units post-capacity; Female condoms: Q3 sales Rs.1Cr due to South African lab breakdown, backlog clearing in Q4; IVD: 8 test kits (pregnancy, malaria), CE/WHO certifications expected in 2-3 years, domestic tenders eligible from Sep 2024-May 2025; Lubricants: bundled with condoms under Cupid brand variants (strawberry, butterscotch, vanilla)
growth verticals / optionality: Acquisition of overseas non-latex (polyisoprene/polyurethane) condom manufacturers in Asia to enter premium segment; expansion into US market via FDA approval (1-1.5 years away); retail distribution scaling in India (1,000+ outlets); IVD entry into African/Latin American markets post-WHO certification
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin: 30.33% (Q3); targeting >35% long-term; PAT margin: low 20s, targeting >25%; cost pressures from USFDA study (requiring US-based trials), inventory write-downs from South African delays; raw material costs stable; logistics costs elevated due to export disruptions
capex / expansion: Land parcel acquired for new facility; capacity expansion to add 300M male condom units by end of FY24; full expansion to Rs.400Cr revenue requires further capex (not quantified); no new capex beyond existing plan mentioned
capital allocation: Rs.385Cr raised via preferential issue to FIIs earmarked for strategic overseas acquisition (condoms/IVD); ESOPs issued to key managerial personnel (not promoters) at Rs.140 exercise price; 50% of warrants to be redistributed to broader employee base; no dividends or buybacks mentioned
risks & watch-items: USFDA approval delayed by 1-1.5 years due to costly US-based trial requirement; South African lab breakdown causing inventory pile-up (Rs.23Cr); acquisition execution risk (timing, integration, regulatory); high inventory days (230+ days, targeting 40-45 day reduction); price sensitivity in India limiting premium condom adoption; currency and geopolitical risks in export markets
management quality / tone: Confident, forward-looking, and disciplined; management emphasizes strategic intent over short-term noise; transparent about delays (South Africa, USFDA); cautious on retail spend; focused on acquisition as core growth lever; tone suggests strong internal alignment and investor communication discipline
non-obvious takeaways: The Rs.385Cr fund raise is not for working capital or capex but for overseas acquisition — a strategic pivot away from pure export manufacturing to vertical integration in premium condom tech; inventory spike is not operational inefficiency but a deliberate stockpile due to export halt, not demand collapse; IVD kits are a hidden growth engine with WHO certification timeline aligning with African government tenders in 2025

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Male condoms: 89% of Q3 sales, 480M unit capacity, expanding to 780M units post-capacity; Female condoms: Q3 sales Rs.1Cr due to South African lab breakdown, backlog clearing in Q4; IVD: 8 test kits (pregnancy, malaria), CE/WHO certifications expected in 2-3 years, domestic tenders eligible from Sep 2024-May 2025; Lubricants: bundled with condoms under Cupid brand variants (strawberry, butterscotch, vanilla)

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Male condoms:** Latex male condoms varied in texture, flavour, shape and size, OEM and private-label male condoms, Flavoured and dotted condoms (launched during FY2026)
- **Female condoms:** WHO/UNFPA pre-qualified natural-rubber-latex female condom, Nitrile (NBR) latex-free female condom (development commenced in FY2026)
- **In-Vitro Diagnostics (IVD) and lubricants:** Pregnancy test kits, HIV 1&2 test kits, Hepatitis B test kits, Syphilis test kits, Malaria test kits, Dengue test kits, COVID-19 antigen test kits, Water-based lubricant sachets / lubricant jelly
- **FMCG, personal care and wellness:** Cupid (premium sexual wellness, fragrances, lubricants, personal care and hygiene), Angel / Cupid Angel (women's sexual wellness, fragrances, body care and beauty), Cupi Safe (menstrual hygiene and wellness), Cupi Kit / CupiKIT (rapid diagnostics), CupiSURE, NiVi, LiVi Home, Eau de parfums, deodorants and pocket perfumes, Face wash, hair-removal sprays, hair and body oils, almond hair oil, petroleum jelly, Toilet sanitisers (home hygiene), Talcum powder, sunscreen, shower gels, body mists, hand washes and colour cosmetics (launched during FY2026)

certifications.title: Quality certifications
certifications.body:
- WHO/UNFPA pre-qualification for male condoms (first company in the world to receive it for both male and female condoms)
- WHO/UNFPA pre-qualification for the natural-rubber-latex female condom (received 2012)
- CE (EU IVDR) certification for several IVD kits, obtained during FY2026
- ISO standards
- GMP-compliant quality-management systems at the Sinnar facility

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Rs.80Cr total (Rs.50Cr male condoms; Rs.30Cr female condoms); 85-90% international, 10-15% domestic; key buyers: UNFPA, Brazilian government (Rs.23Cr tender expected), Government of India (Rs.15Cr awarded + Rs.10Cr expected), South Africa (Rs.50Cr 3-year contract)

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Q4FY24 topline: Rs.50-55Cr; female condom sales: Rs.21Cr; FY24 total revenue: ~Rs.160Cr; FY25 topline target: Rs.400Cr; EBITDA: >Rs.100Cr post-capacity expansion

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Acquisition of overseas non-latex (polyisoprene/polyurethane) condom manufacturers in Asia to enter premium segment; expansion into US market via FDA approval (1-1.5 years away); retail distribution scaling in India (1,000+ outlets); IVD entry into African/Latin American markets post-WHO certification

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- The global condom market is expected to grow at a CAGR of about 8.7% between FY23-30, driven by rising awareness of HIV and other sexually transmitted infections, family-planning programmes and expanding retail and e-commerce access; Asia-Pacific is the largest market at roughly half of global revenue and latex remains the dominant material.
- The female condom market is estimated at approximately 770 million in 2026, growing to around 1.2 billion by 2030, and is increasingly segmenting by material - latex, polyurethane and, at the premium end, nitrile.
- Nitrile products typically command 25-35% higher pricing than latex, the direction in which the company is investing.
- India's IVD market was estimated by IMARC at approximately US$5.3 billion in 2024, growing to around US$10.0 billion by 2033, driven by rising chronic and infectious disease, health awareness, diagnostic access in smaller towns and rural areas, and government focus on public health.
- India's FMCG market was estimated at approximately US$289 billion in 2025 and is expected to reach around US$643 billion by 2030, a CAGR of roughly 17%, with personal care and health-and-wellness among the fastest-growing categories.
- GST rationalisation and simplification together with personal income-tax relief are expected to put more money in the hands of consumers and support demand for everyday products of the kind being built in the consumer business; rural demand showed signs of a durable recovery and inflation remained benign.
- A generally firmer US Dollar against the Indian Rupee supported the reported realisations of exporters, although currency is acknowledged as a two-way risk.
- Operating leverage is the stated margin lever: as volumes scaled, the cost base grew far more slowly, and a favourable export-realisation environment supported margins; management expects margins to remain healthy as scale builds, while noting that quarter-to-quarter mix and the timing of large institutional orders can cause variability.
- Richer product mix and broad-based volume growth across both export and domestic businesses were cited as the drivers of the year's growth.
- A marked increase in tariffs and protectionist measures, and the uncertainty they created, weighed on investment and external demand in several regions - reinforcing the value of a geographically diversified customer base for an export-oriented business.
- Holding raw-material inventory, including crude-linked inputs, for well over six months supports uninterrupted execution and margin resilience.
- CE (EU IVDR) certifications obtained during the year strengthen eligibility for regulated markets and institutional programmes.
- Our institutional order pipeline across government and UN-agency programmes is the strongest it has been.
- Global tenders and institutional demand is listed as an opportunity: a strong and growing order pipeline across governments and UN agencies, supported by pre-qualification status and track record.
- The timing of large institutional orders is flagged as a source of quarter-to-quarter variability, alongside customer and tender concentration in the institutional business.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: EBITDA margin: 30.33% (Q3); targeting >35% long-term; PAT margin: low 20s, targeting >25%; cost pressures from USFDA study (requiring US-based trials), inventory write-downs from South African delays; raw material costs stable; logistics costs elevated due to export disruptions

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Rs.385Cr raised via preferential issue to FIIs earmarked for strategic overseas acquisition (condoms/IVD); ESOPs issued to key managerial personnel (not promoters) at Rs.140 exercise price; 50% of warrants to be redistributed to broader employee base; no dividends or buybacks mentioned

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Cupid's principal growth investment is a new plant at Palava, purpose-built with integrated dual-polymer dipping lines for both natural-rubber-latex and nitrile products. The Executive Director describes Palava as India's first facility capable of manufacturing both natural rubber latex and nitrile condoms on dedicated production lines, while natural rubber latex continues to account for the overwhelming majority of production; the nitrile capability is intended to open a long-term opportunity in the global female-condom market. On full commissioning, total capacity is expected to rise towards approximately 1.25 billion male and 125 million female condoms a year, which management says would make Cupid the only Indian manufacturer across male, female and nitrile female condoms. The stated FY2027 operational priority is to commission the Palava facility on schedule during FY27, alongside establishing the nitrile female condom platform and preparing it for regulated global markets; execution risk on capacity expansion is mitigated by phased commissioning supported by established manufacturing expertise. The established facility at Sinnar, near Nashik, remains the operating base, running GMP-compliant quality-management systems with every condom electronically tested before dispatch. Expansion of market access is being pursued through strategic investments rather than plant alone - the Baazar Style Retail partnership and the GII Healthcare Fund are described as disciplined investments to strengthen market access and expand distribution. Supply security is managed by holding raw-material inventory, including crude-linked inputs, comfortably for well over six months. The annual report gives no rupee capex quantum for Palava in the narrative, and the capital-commitments named disclosure supplied carries no attributable figure.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident, forward-looking, and disciplined; management emphasizes strategic intent over short-term noise; transparent about delays (South Africa, USFDA); cautious on retail spend; focused on acquisition as core growth lever; tone suggests strong internal alignment and investor communication discipline

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Regulatory pre-qualification as an entry barrier: first company in the world to earn WHO/UNFPA pre-qualification for both male and female condoms, a credential described as central to the institutional business
- Rare global position in female condoms - one of only a handful of manufacturers worldwide, supplying more than 50 countries
- Three decades of institutional relationships with governments, ministries of health, UN agencies and procurement bodies, supporting repeat tender participation across 125+ countries
- Fully integrated manufacturing with electronic testing of every condom and GMP-compliant systems accepted by drug regulators worldwide
- OEM capability positioned under the 'Made in India with Japanese Quality' initiative
- One manufacturing, research and quality platform serving two engines - the same certifications that win institutional tenders underwrite the consumer brands
- Deep and widening FMCG distribution: more than 1.5 lakh retail outlets nationwide including over 75,000 chemists and over 47,000 cosmetics outlets, plus over 2,900 modern-trade stores listed and an e-commerce channel that serviced over 52,000 orders
- Balance-sheet strength and supply security - modest borrowings, a net-cash position, and raw-material inventory including crude-linked inputs held for well over six months to protect execution and margins
- CE (EU IVDR) certification broadening eligibility for regulated markets and multilateral health tenders

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: USFDA approval delayed by 1-1.5 years due to costly US-based trial requirement; South African lab breakdown causing inventory pile-up (Rs.23Cr); acquisition execution risk (timing, integration, regulatory); high inventory days (230+ days, targeting 40-45 day reduction); price sensitivity in India limiting premium condom adoption; currency and geopolitical risks in export markets

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: The Rs.385Cr fund raise is not for working capital or capex but for overseas acquisition — a strategic pivot away from pure export manufacturing to vertical integration in premium condom tech; inventory spike is not operational inefficiency but a deliberate stockpile due to export halt, not demand collapse; IVD kits are a hidden growth engine with WHO certification timeline aligning with African government tenders in 2025
